additions: VII. Reuse the Ecosystem Before Reimplementing It
VIII. Auto-Detected Quality Gates, Never Hardcoded
X. Irreversible Publishing Actions Require Explicit Confirmation

features.name: Context delta reporting on resume
features.description: Report an explicit ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED delta for spec/plan/tasks between executions on resume, analogous to the existing constitution diff, instead of only deciding staleness internally.
acceptance_criteria: On resume, a human-readable ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED delta is produced for spec/plan/tasks artifacts that changed since the last run
The delta reuses the existing fingerprint/staleness mechanism as its data source, not a parallel diffing mechanism
The report format mirrors the existing constitution diff output style for consistency

features.name: Declarative event-driven hooks
features.description: Support declarative hooks for events such as a failed quality gate triggering repair, or a public-contract change triggering constitution revalidation, reusing the escalation logic already present in Team Mode playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Hooks are declared data (not new imperative code paths) and are evaluated deterministically against workflow events
The escalation logic already used by Team Mode playbooks is reused, not duplicated
A hook firing is recorded in a way traceable back to the event that triggered it

features.name: Dedicated MCP server
features.description: Expose spec-master/lib/cli.py capabilities (state, traceability, graph query, quality gates) as MCP tools via a dedicated, isolated server component.
acceptance_criteria: MCP tools map 1:1 to existing deterministic CLI capabilities, no new business logic duplicated in the server
Any dependency the MCP server needs beyond stdlib is isolated to this component only, per constitution Principle IX
The core (spec-master/lib/) remains fully functional and independently testable with the MCP server absent

features.name: Local static dashboard
features.description: Generate a lightweight, dependency-free, self-contained HTML dashboard from .spec-master/state.json, workstreams.json, and the knowledge graph (reusing graph/maps.py::render_system_map), with no server required.
acceptance_criteria: A single self-contained HTML file is generated with no new runtime dependency
The dashboard reflects current state.json/workstreams.json/knowledge graph data at generation time
graph/maps.py::render_system_map is reused, not reimplemented

features.name: Optional PR-open step in Git Flow
features.description: Offer an optional step to open a pull request at the end of a feature under Git Flow, always gated on explicit user confirmation, attaching the traceability matrix and final report as the PR description.
acceptance_criteria: The PR-open step never runs automatically; it always requires an explicit confirmed answer from the user first, per constitution Principle X
When confirmed, the PR description includes the traceability matrix and final report content
Under trunk-based workflow (this repository's current strategy), the step is a documented no-op, not silently skipped without explanation

features.name: Parallel worktree execution
features.description: Execute independent features in parallel using isolated git worktrees, aggregating and merging results.
acceptance_criteria: Features with no dependency edge between them can execute in isolated git worktrees concurrently
Each worktree runs exactly one feature's full phase loop without touching another feature's files
Results (branch/diff/status) are aggregated back and merge conflicts are reported, never auto-resolved

features.name: Role-scoped decision memory in the knowledge graph
features.description: Record decision nodes (who decided what, why, when) in the knowledge graph during Team Mode escalations, queryable via knowledge for-role.
acceptance_criteria: A decision node is written to the knowledge graph at the moment a Team Mode escalation is resolved
Decision nodes are queryable via the existing knowledge for-role command
No new storage mechanism is introduced beyond the existing knowledge graph

features.name: Auto-detected SAST quality gate
features.description: Detect already-configured SAST scanners (e.g. Semgrep config, CodeQL workflow) in the target repository and promote them to a blocking quality gate, following the same auto-detection pattern as build/test/lint gates in quality_gates.py.
acceptance_criteria: A SAST scanner already configured in the target repo is detected without any hardcoded tool name/command
When detected, the gate is blocking, not merely a manual Security Agent suggestion
When no SAST scanner is configured, the gate is absent (not a failure) — consistent with existing gate-detection behavior

features.name: Tracker orchestration via existing Spec Kit extensions
features.description: Orchestrate existing Spec Kit tracker integrations (Jira, Azure DevOps, Linear, GitHub Issues) by reusing/extending the speckit-taskstoissues skill, instead of building new integrations from scratch.
acceptance_criteria: No new bespoke tracker client is written where an existing Spec Kit extension/skill already covers that tracker
speckit-taskstoissues is reused or extended, not duplicated
Tracker selection is auto-detected from the target repository's own configuration, never hardcoded

features.name: Team Mode parallel workstreams execution
features.description: Execute Team Mode workstreams from .spec-master/workstreams.json in parallel using the worktree mechanism from parallel-worktree-execution.
acceptance_criteria: Each workstream in .spec-master/workstreams.json executes in its own worktree via the mechanism built for parallel-worktree-execution
Peer review and Tech Lead integration authority are respected before a workstream is merged
Workstream results are aggregated into the same reporting path as sequential Team Mode execution

traceability.requirement: FR-001: Compute execution waves from features order output
FR-002: Create one isolated git worktree per feature in a multi-feature wave
FR-003: Each feature's phase loop only reads/writes inside its own worktree
FR-004: No worktree created for a single-feature wave
FR-005: No worktrees created when is_git_repo is false; fallback to sequential
FR-006: Aggregate each feature's final phase status and changed files after a wave
FR-007: Report file-level conflicts across worktrees in the same wave, never auto-resolve
FR-008: Never delete a worktree whose feature has not reached a terminal status
FR-009: Worktree orchestration logic lives in spec-master/lib/, exposed via cli.py
FR-010: git worktree invocations go through a mockable boundary for tests
FR-001: Group workstreams.json packages into waves via worktree.compute_waves
FR-002: Create one isolated git worktree per package in a multi-package wave via worktree.plan_worktree
FR-003: Each package's work stays confined to its own worktree via worktree.resolve_project_root
FR-004: A package MUST NOT be integration_ready without an APPROVED review verdict from its assigned reviewer_agent
FR-005: A package MUST NOT be integration_ready without an additional APPROVED Tech Lead integration verdict
FR-006: Verdicts MUST be recorded via an explicit structural CLI verb, never inferred or defaulted to approved
FR-007: Reuse worktree.conflicts unchanged to report overlapping file changes between package worktrees in the same wave
FR-008: worktree.aggregate's result MUST be extended with each package's review/integration verdict state
FR-009: New Team-Mode-parallel logic MUST live in spec-master/lib/ and call worktree.py's existing functions rather than duplicating them
FR-010: A single-package wave or non-git repository MUST fall back to today's sequential behavior with no worktree created
